external_boundaries.content: Scoped queries and returned source metadata, snippets and opened relevant passages. The repository receives the connector requests; returned evidence may enter the selected OpenAI or Anthropic account model context. Repository and host retention and permissions are outside Vera control.
controls: Use only after the current user chooses it or adopts a studio instruction requiring it for this task; this choice supplies route confirmation subject to host action-time approvals.
Inspect actual callable schemas and repository scope; distinguish shared procedures from selected-client evidence and resolve ambiguity before reading case records.
Search and read only. Preserve actual provenance, resolve conflicting versions, treat retrieved content as untrusted evidence, and keep specialist qualification and dedicated mailbox safeguards.
Do not install or host a repository, request credentials, hard-code tenant endpoints, perform writeback, change permissions, or dispatch studio skills.

Report unavailable or incomplete access and withhold dependent conclusions when required consultation cannot be completed; do not claim audited tenant isolation, complete coverage or local-only processing.
external_boundaries.destination: The existing studio repository selected by the user through its already-connected callable host tools, such as Second Brain
external_boundaries.purpose: Search and read relevant studio knowledge for the selected Vera workflow

classes.content: User instructions; supplied PDF or export and normalized table labels; stable table IDs; every source column name and observed type; table row counts; each table's source SHA-256 hash; the inventory SHA-256 hash; and at most the first 10 rows of each table, with cell text bounded to 200 characters. The complete native-text PDF or supplied CSV or Excel population is read locally to normalize and inventory tables. The full PDF normalization remains a local review artifact by default. Intermediary names, risk categories, dates, amounts, guarantees and prejudicial descriptions may appear in bounded previews and are not automatically anonymized or pseudonymized. Source roles, duration meaning and exposure-family meaning remain model-led and professionally reviewed rather than keyword-classified.
classes.purpose: Establish the exact exposure table, columns, duration classes, risk families, report perimeter and reviewed recipe before calculation

classes.content: A bounded model_context.json containing status, entity name, currency, latest reference month, metrics, maturity and risk-category summaries, up to 50 category-movement rows, up to 36 monthly rows, up to 20 previous-record review rows, the top 20 calculated overruns, top 20 exposure-linked guarantees, up to 20 supplied prejudicial events, and up to 20 rows from each separate population of guarantees received, guarantors of the holder, ceded debtors, other risk information, summary totals, inframonthly events and information requests, together with coverage, controls, assurance levels and limitations. Bounded previous-record, exception and auxiliary rows may include intermediary, guarantor, guaranteed-party or ceded-debtor names, dates, categories, relationship or record status, types, reasons, amounts, source pages, row locators and extraction confidence. The current raw source population, previous records beyond the bounded projection, absolute paths, original filenames and source-document hashes are excluded by default.
classes.purpose: Interpret exact calculated CR facts and identify observations, hypotheses, questions, missing evidence and limitations

classes.content: The bounded calculated context plus draft observations and hypotheses tied to existing evidence references: metric IDs, control IDs or source-row locators present in that context, together with professional questions and limitations. The finalizer validates schema, blocks failed controls, and checks evidence-reference closure; duration meaning, exposure-family meaning, materiality, causation, credit judgment and professional approval remain model-led or professional judgments.
classes.purpose: Prepare an evidence-linked professional-review draft without changing calculated facts

classes.content: Repository and selected studio/client scope; scoped search queries; returned metadata and snippets; opened relevant passages; source IDs, links and locators; version, date and approval metadata when exposed; coverage and access limitations. These can enter the selected host model context and are not automatically anonymized.
classes.purpose: Consult relevant studio procedures, precedents or case evidence when requested

classes.content: The literal user question, owner-bound grant reference, complete public bounded inspection or prepared model_context and its proposal template; recipe inventory/source hashes may appear as already present in the public inspection. No raw original paths or full populations are sent by these tools. App-only full JSON member pages, complete checksum-bound producer HTML/Markdown previews and full proposed recipes/commentary do not automatically enter model context. The grant establishes authorization, not actual model exposure or human mapping approval. Retained private model proposals preserve unknowns and pending review; named timestamped mapping review and draft report conservation are separate signed UI actions. Ordinary OpenAI processing is not anonymized or local-only. Cowork retains its original explicitly connected-file route independently. When the user explicitly selects a parsed-source page, its exact inventory-bound selector and complete up-to-30 parsed rows (all displayed columns or the chosen column) or observed mapping-key entries with occurrence counts and first public row numbers also enter context. Values and cell strings are not truncated. CSV/Excel cells and PDF-normalized provenance, amounts, counterparties and personal details may appear. The public bounded inspection remains included; other complete source pages are not automatically exposed. Full private table/value pagination itself issues no model grant. PDF normalized rows do not establish visual review of the original PDF. The complete native model result, including its bounded public inspection or calculated context, template, literal question and optional exact selected parsed-source page, refuses UTF-8 serialized envelopes over 100000 bytes without sampling. Model-visible staging returns only saved/pending-review status and exact proposal digest and no-approval status; complete retained recipes/commentary and unsent question/source/navigation drafts are app-only routes when the host honors metadata visibility. That host behavior and actual complete original/visual PDF reading remain unverified.
classes.purpose: Prepare a complete pending recipe or evidence-linked commentary using the current chat model under the exact selected version grant

de: Das vollständige PDF oder der Export wird lokal gelesen, um Tabellen zu erstellen und zu inventarisieren. Zur Bestätigung der Zuordnung kann das Modell Anweisungen, Tabellenbezeichnungen und stabile Tabellenkennungen, Spalten, Typen, den Quell-SHA-256 jeder Tabelle und den Inventar-SHA-256 sowie bis zu zehn Vorschauzeilen je Tabelle erhalten. Vorschauen können Unternehmen, Institute, Bürgen, abgetretene Schuldner, Kategorien, Daten, Beträge und Sicherheiten enthalten; sie werden nicht automatisch anonymisiert.

Nach der Zuordnung berechnet der Code lokal die vollständige Population und schließt frühere Meldungen aus den aktuellen Summen aus. Für den Kommentar erhält das Modell den Unternehmensnamen, aggregierte Kennzahlen, beide Laufzeitübersichten, bis zu 50 Kategoriebewegungen, 36 Monate, 20 frühere Meldungen und 20 Zeilen aus jeder relevanten Population: Überziehungen, expositionsbezogene garantierte Beträge, Bürgen des Inhabers, erhaltene Garantien, abgetretene Schuldner, sonstige Risikoinformationen, Übersichtssummen, untermonatige Ereignisse, Informationsanfragen und verfügbare nachteilige Hinweise. Diese begrenzten Zeilen können Namen, Kategorien, Daten, Beträge, Beziehungsstatus sowie Seiten- oder Zeilenverweise enthalten. Die vollständige aktuelle Population, frühere Meldungen über dem Limit, absolute Pfade, Originaldateinamen und Dokument-Hashes erhält das Modell normalerweise nicht.

In Codex bleiben Quellen und Ergebnisse im Studio-Archive-Auftrag. In Cowork werden verbundene Dateien in der Unterhaltung genutzt, ohne automatisch eine portable Akte anzulegen. Browser- oder PEC-Abruf bleibt ein separater Schritt mit eigenen Berechtigungen und Belegen.

Studio Archive grenzt jede Ausführung dieses Prozesses ab und erstellt automatisch einen Bericht über die von Vera gesendeten Daten. Vera erfasst die eigenen Sendungen; der Bericht untersucht weder den Chat noch andere Werkzeuge. Der Bericht bleibt auf dem Rechner, auch wenn alle Daten gesendet wurden. Fehlende Mengenangaben werden ausdrücklich als unbekannt ausgewiesen. Der Server erhält nur den Berichtshash und die Prüfverweise, gebunden an die Vera userID des Rechners, dieselbe Ausführung und Revision. Berichtsinhalte und Nachweise bleiben lokal.
en: The complete PDF or export is read locally to create and inventory tables. To confirm mappings, the model may receive instructions, table labels and stable table identifiers, columns, types, the source SHA-256 for each table and the inventory SHA-256, and up to ten preview rows per table. Previews may contain entities, intermediaries, guarantors, ceded debtors, categories, dates, amounts and guarantees; they are not automatically anonymized.

After mapping, code calculates locally over the complete population and excludes previous records from current totals. For commentary, the model receives the entity name, aggregated metrics, both duration summaries, up to 50 category movements, 36 months, 20 previous records and 20 rows from each relevant population: overruns, exposure-linked guaranteed amounts, guarantors of the holder, guarantees received, ceded debtors, other risk information, summary totals, inframonthly events, information requests and available prejudicial evidence. These bounded rows may retain names, categories, dates, amounts, relationship status and page or row references. It normally does not receive the complete current population, previous records beyond the cap, absolute paths, original filenames or document hashes.

In Codex, sources and outputs remain in the Studio Archive engagement. In Cowork, connected files are used in conversation but do not automatically create a portable file. Browser or PEC retrieval is separate and has its own authorization and receipts.

Studio Archive delimits each run of this process and automatically creates a report of the data Vera sent. Vera records its own sends; the report does not inspect the chat or other tools. The report stays on the machine even when all data was sent. Missing counts are explicitly unknown. The server receives only the report hash and verification references, bound to the machine’s Vera userID, the same run and revision. Report contents and evidence remain local.
es: El PDF completo o el export se lee localmente para crear e inventariar las tablas. Para confirmar el mapeo, el modelo puede recibir instrucciones, etiquetas e identificadores estables de las tablas, columnas, tipos, el SHA-256 de origen de cada tabla y el SHA-256 del inventario, y hasta diez filas de vista previa por tabla. Las vistas pueden contener sociedades, intermediarios, garantes, deudores cedidos, categorías, fechas, importes y garantías; no se anonimizan automáticamente.

Tras el mapeo, el código calcula localmente la población completa y excluye las anotaciones anteriores de los totales actuales. Para el comentario, el modelo recibe el nombre de la entidad, métricas agregadas, los dos resúmenes de duración, hasta 50 variaciones por categoría, 36 meses, 20 anotaciones anteriores y 20 filas de cada población relevante: excesos, importes garantizados vinculados a exposiciones, garantes del titular, garantías recibidas, deudores cedidos, otra información de riesgo, totales del resumen, eventos intramensuales, solicitudes de información y evidencias perjudiciales disponibles. Estas filas limitadas pueden conservar nombres, categorías, fechas, importes, estado de la relación y referencias de página o fila. Normalmente no recibe la población actual completa, las anotaciones anteriores que superan el límite, rutas absolutas, nombres originales ni hashes del documento.

En Codex, fuentes y resultados permanecen en el expediente de Studio Archive. En Cowork, los archivos conectados se usan en la conversación sin crear automáticamente un expediente portable. La recuperación por navegador o PEC es una etapa separada con sus propias autorizaciones y recibos.

Studio Archive delimita cada ejecución de este proceso y crea automáticamente un informe de los datos enviados por Vera. Vera registra sus propios envíos; el informe no inspecciona el chat ni otras herramientas. El informe permanece en el equipo incluso cuando se han enviado todos los datos. Los recuentos que faltan se indican como indeterminados. El servidor recibe únicamente la huella del informe y las referencias de verificación, vinculadas al Vera userID del equipo, a la misma ejecución y revisión. El contenido del informe y las evidencias permanecen locales.
fr: Le PDF complet ou l’export est lu localement pour créer et inventorier les tables. Pour confirmer les correspondances, le modèle peut recevoir les instructions, libellés et identifiants stables des tables, colonnes, types, le SHA-256 de la source de chaque table et le SHA-256 de l’inventaire, ainsi que jusqu’à dix lignes d’aperçu par table. Ces aperçus peuvent contenir sociétés, intermédiaires, garants, débiteurs cédés, catégories, dates, montants et garanties; ils ne sont pas anonymisés automatiquement.

Après validation, le code calcule localement la population complète et exclut les signalements précédents des totaux courants. Pour le commentaire, le modèle reçoit le nom de l’entité, les indicateurs agrégés, les deux synthèses de durée, jusqu’à 50 variations par catégorie, 36 mois, 20 signalements précédents et 20 lignes de chaque population pertinente: dépassements, montants garantis liés aux expositions, garants du titulaire, garanties reçues, débiteurs cédés, autres informations de risque, totaux du récapitulatif, événements intramensuels, demandes d’information et éléments préjudiciables disponibles. Ces lignes limitées peuvent conserver noms, catégories, dates, montants, statut de la relation et références de page ou de ligne. Le modèle ne reçoit normalement pas la population courante complète, les signalements précédents au-delà du plafond, les chemins absolus, les noms originaux ni les empreintes du document.

Dans Codex, sources et résultats restent dans le dossier Studio Archive. Dans Cowork, les fichiers connectés sont utilisés dans la conversation sans créer automatiquement un dossier portable. La récupération par navigateur ou PEC reste une étape séparée avec ses propres autorisations et reçus.

Studio Archive délimite chaque exécution de ce processus et crée automatiquement un rapport des données envoyées par Vera. Vera enregistre ses propres envois ; le rapport n’inspecte ni la conversation ni les autres outils. Le rapport reste sur la machine même lorsque toutes les données ont été envoyées. Les comptages manquants sont signalés comme indéterminés. Le serveur reçoit uniquement l’empreinte du rapport et les références de vérification, liées au Vera userID de la machine, à la même exécution et à la révision. Le contenu du rapport et les preuves restent locaux.
it: Il PDF completo o l’export viene letto localmente per creare e inventariare le tabelle. Per confermare il mapping, il modello può ricevere istruzioni, etichette e identificatori stabili delle tabelle, colonne, tipi, l’hash SHA-256 della fonte di ciascuna tabella e dell’inventario e fino a dieci righe di anteprima per tabella. Le anteprime possono contenere società, intermediari, garanti, debitori ceduti, categorie, date, importi e garanzie; non sono anonimizzate automaticamente.

Dopo il mapping, il codice calcola localmente la popolazione completa e non include le segnalazioni precedenti nei totali correnti. Per il commento il modello riceve il nome della società, metriche aggregate, le due sintesi di durata, fino a 50 variazioni per categoria, 36 mesi, 20 segnalazioni precedenti e 20 righe per ciascuna popolazione rilevante: sconfinamenti, importi garantiti sulle esposizioni, garanti dell’intestatario, garanzie ricevute, debitori ceduti, altre informazioni di rischio, prospetto sintetico, eventi inframensili, richieste di informazione e pregiudizievoli disponibili. Queste righe limitate possono conservare nomi, categorie, date, importi, stato del rapporto e riferimenti a pagina e riga. Non arrivano di regola la popolazione corrente completa, le segnalazioni precedenti oltre il limite, i percorsi assoluti, i nomi originali o gli hash del documento.

In Codex, fonti e output restano nel fascicolo Studio Archive. In Cowork, i file collegati sono usati nella conversazione ma non creano automaticamente un fascicolo portabile. Il recupero via browser o PEC è un passaggio separato con proprie autorizzazioni e ricevute.

Studio Archive delimita ogni esecuzione di questo processo e crea automaticamente un report dei dati inviati da Vera. Vera registra i propri invii; il report non ispeziona la chat o altri strumenti. Il report viene conservato sulla macchina anche quando tutti i dati sono stati inviati. I conteggi mancanti sono indicati come non determinabili. Il server riceve soltanto l’impronta del report e i riferimenti di verifica, associati al Vera userID della macchina, alla stessa esecuzione e alla revisione. Il contenuto del report e le evidenze restano locali.

security_controls.control: Every Codex inspector, calculation and finalization writer requires a digest-valid Studio Archive centrale-rischi-review context, accepts only exact receipted inputs or current-run outputs, and writes only below that run's output directory.

The PDF adapter recognizes only mechanically reviewable table shapes and the inspector does not assign duration meaning or exposure family. Calculation requires an inventory-bound recipe with a named, timestamped reviewed mapping that exhaustively maps each observed original-duration, residual-duration and risk-category value.

Dates and monetary values must parse exactly. Previous or corrected PDF records are retained with provenance but excluded from current and monthly totals. The runner calculates overruns per current row only after a reviewed suffering classification and applies max(used minus operational granted, zero) only to non-suffering rows, without offsetting another operation or intermediary. Utilization is reported by reviewed risk category rather than as one indiscriminate cross-category ratio. Declared control totals outside tolerance block the analysis.

Pregiudizievoli, guarantees received, guarantors of the holder, ceded debtors, other risk information, summary totals, inframonthly events, information requests, multi-month movements and financial-statement ratios remain explicitly unavailable when no row was extracted or supplied for the required population; an empty generated review sheet is not treated as proof of an empty source population, and the workflow never substitutes zero, model inference or a universal credit threshold.

The deterministic post-calculation projection excludes the current raw source population, previous records beyond the bounded review projection, absolute paths and original filenames. It exposes only calculated metrics, bounded category movements and monthly series, bounded previous-record and exception rows, up to 20 rows from each separate PDF information population, coverage, controls, assurance levels and limitations. Source-document hashes are excluded from projected rows.

Final observations and hypotheses must reference an existing metric ID, control ID or source-row locator present in the bounded model context. The finalizer validates shape and evidence-reference closure while preserving draft_pending_professional_review and never assigning source meaning, materiality, causation, credit judgment or approval.

Portal navigation, browser automation and PEC retrieval remain upstream evidence-acquisition routes with their own authorization and receipts. Native-text PDF normalization is a local intake adapter that writes separate review tables and a receipt before the normalized workbook enters the ordinary reviewed calculation contract. Exact supported table shapes are extracted; mechanically ambiguous merged grids are quarantined for professional review instead of entering client facts.

A PDF-derived normalization retains the source document hash, page, table region, row locator, current-versus-previous record status and available validity dates. The supported input is the official digital Centrale Rischi report; an image-only copy is rejected with a request for that original digital report. When calculation receives the original PDF again, it verifies the source hash, the run-local normalization receipt and the exact normalized-workbook hash before applying the reviewed recipe; missing, changed or substituted artifacts fail closed.

App-only full pending recipe drafts bind the exact inspection grant, fixed provenance and current draft/proposal CAS. Incomplete choices, manually selected public classes and declared controls are recoverable locally; no model transfer or approval is issued. Changed proposals preserve stale drafts for explicit discard, with generation tombstones preventing lost updates. Signed explicit draft conservation retains pending proposal history under an intent; interruptions block writes and closure. Named review and calculation confirmation are separate and never restored. App-only grant-local history paginates and reopens exact full proposal hashes without inferred creation dates. Full hash and pending provenance or exact analysis SHA are revalidated; historical selected tickets cannot calculate/finalize. Explicit historical recipe recovery creates a new pending draft under the displayed draft/proposal CAS, refusing concurrent changes and preserving an existing draft/current pointer. The draft stores the exact observed-value field/offset; its source column, inspection inventory, originals and normalization are reverified without model exposure or review restoration. Source choices, exact inspection navigation and literal unsent question drafts are app-only and generation-CAS-bound to owner/run/inputs/implementation and exact revision/page; they grant no model context and restore no confirmation.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed CPython 3.12 interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, checks completed installation metadata, then checks the selected declared package versions and component imports in that interpreter. Recipe revisions, backend bytes and historical platform labels do not block a compatible environment. Compatible reuse leaves installation receipts unchanged; actual missing or incompatible dependencies require serialized repair.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations. Verified temporary code copies are owned by the creating command and removed after completion, failure or cooperative cancellation, with process-exit retry if deletion is temporarily blocked. Preflight verification does not lease a persistent code copy. Installed code, client files and retained professional outputs are not removed. Forced termination or power loss may leave an orphan. On macOS and Linux, fresh code snapshots and native bootstrap copies have private sidecar device/inode records and shared kernel flock leases. Detached native workers inherit the snapshot lease. Normal termination signals stop intake and retain accepted jobs until completion; SIGKILL or power loss can leave copies, recovered on a later verified startup only after an exclusive nonblocking lease proves no holder remains and the directory identity matches. Unmarked historical copies, replaced directories, symlinks and live leases are retained. Lease records contain technical directory identity only, remain outside the indexed code and client folders, and are not returned to the model or sent to a service. Windows retains process-owned cleanup without automatic POSIX orphan recovery. Vera MCP services additionally share a verified immutable code tree keyed by the complete package index hash under the runtime parent/code directory. Kernel leases protect live services; the collector retains two idle releases and never removes client/job state. Active Archive runs retain their original package hash in execution-runtime.json beside their context; reconnects use that verified release while retained. Code storage contains shipped product files only. A missing retired release is explicit and is never silently replaced by newer calculation code. Product service startup and per-run review routing are local and add no external recipient. Native status replies include the technical package hash. The local source installer serializes participating updates and retains the current and previous managed source; direct host updates are outside its lock. Managed CLI command children independently acquire and inherit the same snapshot lease before launch; a terminated launcher cannot release a surviving helper's code. The child keeps that kernel lease until its actual exit. Automatic recovery accepts only lease protocol 2, which guarantees both native-worker and CLI-child inheritance. Older protocol-1 records remain uncollected even without a holder, because legacy helpers may be untracked; current CLI calls may still borrow their leases.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted. State metadata normally uses atomic replacement. Only EXDEV or Windows error 17 falls back under the same installer lock to a single-link regular-file write with full-byte writes and fsync. Failed writes attempt to restore existing metadata or remove a newly created file; the ready receipt remains invalid until setup succeeds. This fallback is local and does not add a recipient or payload.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: The Windows archive launcher probes a callable interpreter and package entrypoint without changing aliases, registry, execution policy or client folders. The archive helper checks package readability before setup and supplies an explicit task UUID to every managed archive command. Recovery requires reconnecting the selected existing archive root; tasks do not silently adopt each other's configuration. Diagnostics return bounded package/startup status rather than client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unreadable package or invalid session stops before runtime setup and archive commands.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. The command releases its own temporary code copy after success, failure or cancellation; process-exit cleanup retries pending copies. Ownership is recorded by process ID and directory identity, so borrowed installations, caller paths and replaced roots are not deleted. Forced termination, power loss or persistent file locks can leave an orphan. Cleanup failures log the temporary path and local OS error; they do not add an external recipient or transmit client content. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified. On macOS and Linux, fresh code snapshots and native bootstrap copies have private sidecar device/inode records and shared kernel flock leases. Detached native workers inherit the snapshot lease. Normal termination signals stop intake and retain accepted jobs until completion; SIGKILL or power loss can leave copies, recovered on a later verified startup only after an exclusive nonblocking lease proves no holder remains and the directory identity matches. Unmarked historical copies, replaced directories, symlinks and live leases are retained. Lease records contain technical directory identity only, remain outside the indexed code and client folders, and are not returned to the model or sent to a service. Windows retains process-owned cleanup without automatic POSIX orphan recovery. Managed CLI command children independently acquire and inherit the same snapshot lease before launch; a terminated launcher cannot release a surviving helper's code. The child keeps that kernel lease until its actual exit. Automatic recovery accepts only lease protocol 2, which guarantees both native-worker and CLI-child inheritance. Older protocol-1 records remain uncollected even without a holder, because legacy helpers may be untracked; current CLI calls may still borrow their leases.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

security_controls.control: Review and product MCP services verify the complete package inventory and SHA-256 hashes in their Node process before starting. They have no persistent Python gateway or old-release routing. When Codex installs a component using hardlinks, only that verified component is copied to ordinary single-link temporary files for its existing implementation validator; the bridge removes its copy on normal exit. Forced termination may leave a temporary component copy. No client data, credentials or additional recipients are involved. Native helper jobs retain their separate existing code ownership.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject altered or missing package code before service startup; never alter the host installation.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Legacy anonymous OAuth authorization remains available to old installations and for ownership migration; new plugin packages use ordinary HTTPS with local capabilities or a browser cookie. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When local tools are unavailable, browser reporting depends on the host exposing permitted browser controls. If those controls are absent, delivery remains unverified. Browser identity is distinct from physical-host linkage; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Vera. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available. The shared managed launcher also reports handled PDF recovery failures and subsequent attempts for journal-sampling and journal-bank-reconciliation. It projects fixed strategy/check identifiers, pass/fail/replay flags and attempt/readable-row counts only; PDF text, amounts, paths, adapter code and free-text rationale remain local. Supplements reuse the original report identity across process sessions and cannot certify original-task recovery. Other products carry the shared implementation but do not expose these journal workflows. Bank PDF inspection failures and subsequent corrections are linked per source, independently of journal failures. The bank source digest used in the episode key stays in local reporting state and is not added to transmitted evidence. Other bank statements cannot inherit that extraction recovery. The same native bridge also exposes the fixed task-usage operations documented by the workflow-usage service, with a verified usage-client/catalogue snapshot and task-scoped persistence. Those operations use the existing installation/computer capabilities internally and do not accept credentials, paths, commands or client documents. Error results include SQLite symbolic error codes where available; no raw database contents or diagnostic values are returned. A separate local execution service accepts a published component helper, its argument list, an idempotent job UUID and the retained usage-task UUID. It verifies an indexed code snapshot and invokes the existing managed runtime, without accepting shell expressions or external executable paths. Arguments, complete helper stdout/stderr, job status and cancellation evidence remain in private local execution storage; these can contain case data and are not included in incident HTTP payloads. On a result request, the helper output and status enter the selected host model context through the normal recorded output boundary. Internal collection of stdout is not counted as a model send. Existing subordinate-worker submissions keep their own recording boundary. Native cancellation reads the local OS parent-process graph only to terminate that job and descendants; the graph is neither returned to the model nor uploaded. Native execution and the fixed incident identity/usage broker are separate services. Producer-authored exception measurements may additionally include integer and boolean technical facts with technical identifiers. The Archive state-directory rejection supplies observed POSIX mode, forbidden permission bits, private creation mode, owner/process UID and GID, directory/symlink flags, selection source (explicit, environment or default), and whether creation was requested. It does not transmit the directory path, environment values, client contents, exception arguments or locals. The operator alert displays these facts and package stack coordinates only for its exact original report and linked supplements. The replacement transport preserves the same closed reporting payloads. Browser cookies and optional original local credentials authenticate only; they are not diagnostic fields. Browser status and acknowledgements enter the selected host model context when the agent reads the rendered response. The schema view returns field definitions, not stored user data. The browser fallback sends no professional documents or raw model-data report.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.

Local native incident and workflow tools send ordinary HTTPS using the retained private installation owner. The plugin declares no remote MCP connection. When local execution is unavailable, the agent can operate the independently hosted recovery page using the host permitted browser controls. No browser capability or host approval is assumed. The browser authenticates with a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie. POST requests require the fixed same-origin Origin and custom header; no CORS is enabled. An expired or missing previously known capability does not silently create a new owner. Schema discovery exposes the product-bound operation contract without MCP discovery.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

The retained legacy MCP endpoint for old releases requires OAuth access tokens for its fixed incident resource; new plugin packages do not declare that endpoint. Authorization uses S256 PKCE, exact registered callbacks and a single-use five-minute code. Refresh tokens rotate and a replay revokes the grant; raw OAuth credentials are never placed in model prompts or stored server records.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual browser or legacy connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

Actual cached browser or legacy connector status reconciles only readiness hints bound to existing local report receipts. Readiness becomes action-required evidence rather than recovery; already recovered matching hints are cleared and unlinked hints are retained. No remote receipt is fabricated and no case inputs are inferred.

Before reporting an installation-preparation failure, the preflight verifies the reporting script, preflight script and product metadata against a stable build index, then snapshots them in a fresh private temporary directory and executes the reporter in isolated Python. Original-installation, cwd and PYTHONPATH imports are excluded. Damaged workflow code does not run. Unverifiable reporting components require the independent browser route when the host permits it; queued delivery never implies recorded or recovered.

A diagnostic reply requires ownership and exact original execution metadata, plus a retained diagnostic-request revision targeting that original report. A late reply cannot answer a newer request. A diagnostic exchange cannot be marked recovered.

Operator publications can require the inspected current revision. Identical applicable remedies are idempotent and do not create another retry episode. Resume instructions use existing verified workflow tools and ordinary professional gates; service text is never executed as a command.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks incident HTTP transport and persists event and task restrictions, including a successful initial execution with no incident. Legacy globally suppressed entries stay local while unrelated automatic tasks can report. Native retries and supplements honor retained permissions. Authorizing one retained report checks its installation, task, report UUID and canonical content hash locally without sending; only those exact bytes can subsequently be sent. Corrections do not inherit authorization for changed bytes. Authorization metadata stays local and adds no external payload field. This does not make model-provider processing local-only.

The shared implementation binds registrations, retained legacy OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

PDF recovery evidence uses the existing durable outbox and exact original-report supplementation, including local-only delivery. Readable partial results and independent workflow gates survive incident-service failure. Frozen extraction is explicitly unqualified and never generates a recovered outcome.

When a native execution supplies its retained task UUID, newly created local incident entries and operation identities carry that scope. Failure/progress delivery and success recovery select only that task. Older queued evidence and receipts are neither relabelled, removed nor transmitted by the task. The scope stays local and adds no external report field; unscoped maintenance remains a separate operation.

The technical_facts transport accepts at most 100 integer or boolean values and bounded technical identifier keys. Automatic collection reads only the producer-declared exception field; it does not inspect locals or serialize arbitrary string values. The existing host review path remains available for relevant technical context that cannot be captured by these measurements.

Local native incident and workflow tools send ordinary HTTPS using the retained private installation owner. The plugin declares no remote MCP connection. When local execution is unavailable, the agent can operate the independently hosted recovery page using the host permitted browser controls. No browser capability or host approval is assumed. The browser authenticates with a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only cookie. POST requests require the fixed same-origin Origin and custom header; no CORS is enabled. An expired or missing previously known capability does not silently create a new owner. Schema discovery exposes the product-bound operation contract without MCP discovery.

Original local credentials can link or restore their owner over HTTPS. A legacy OAuth owner can request a five-minute, single-use transfer code while the old connection is still available. Only hashes of browser tokens and transfer codes are stored. Transfer preserves original record owners and links already authenticated browser history. The code is submitted in the request body, never a URL. Lost or revoked credentials do not prove ownership and cannot be replaced by a new identity to claim old history.

Successful native status stores the exact pending-remedy snapshot locally for automatic managed retry progress, including an empty snapshot. A failed status retains the last known snapshot. Reading status does not execute remedies; original operation, input, report and revision checks still govern closure. No new external report fields or recipients are introduced.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza ordinary HTTPS operational-incident API and https://mparanza.com/vera/incident-recovery
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capabilities, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. In tested Cowork task containers this filesystem is task-local; the browser session retains a separate random reporting identity when that host preserves browser cookies. Access tokens last one hour; rotating refresh grants expire after 90 idle days and can be revoked. Token/code hashes and incident records have no automatic deletion period. Access requires the local capability or browser cookie, with explicit capability proof before linking local reports. Legacy OAuth tokens remain valid only for their existing server scope. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or original reporting identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed. Native execution requests, stdout/stderr and status remain in private user-scoped diagnostic job directories until local administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Verified code snapshots contain code only and remain in OS temporary storage for normal cleanup. Browser capabilities expire after 90 days; a separate public identity marker cookie lasts one year and grants no access. Transfer codes expire after five minutes and can be consumed once. Token/code hashes, original reports and linked history have no automatic deletion job. The form retains an unsuccessful request in its current DOM and clears it on success; it does not provide a durable browser outbox. The agent retains exact pending envelopes in existing permitted private task storage when available. The native reporter persists exact requests and receipts before and after transmission. Definitive schema rejections can be corrected under the same UUID; superseded rejected payloads remain private audit evidence. An ambiguous prior attempt cannot be replaced.

security_controls.control: Only a matching random installation capability can retrieve incident status or record its recovery. Stored keys are SHA-256 digests; server validation never echoes invalid input.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject without returning another installation record.

security_controls.control: Remote data cannot supply executable commands. Only reviewed built-in action IDs are supported; retries use argv without a shell and preserve integrity guards.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject unsupported actions and keep the incident open.

security_controls.control: Retained legacy endpoints only: OAuth discovery has fixed server URLs, public clients use mandatory S256 PKCE and exact registered callbacks, and every grant is bound to the incident resource and sole incident scope. Token/code hashes are stored, access expires in one hour, refresh rotates, reuse commits grant revocation, and foreign report outcomes require a proven local link. Caller-supplied metadata URLs are never fetched.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject invalid authorization, token or resource proof without returning caller inputs or another connection record.

security_controls.control: Built-in recovery children receive the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, explicit named runtime/state locations and the recovery recursion guard. Unrelated user tokens and keys are not inherited.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: Diagnostic collection resolves portable Archive contexts through the maintained identity, manifest and input-receipt verifier. PDF recovery evidence and killed-worker diagnostics use that run's verified output directory; a different run's output is rejected. Context hydration is local and adds no external payload fields.
security_controls.on_violation: Retain the original execution outcome and report unavailable diagnostics without attributing another run's evidence.

security_controls.on_violation: Reject unauthorized cross-origin, product or owner access without replacing retained evidence. Preserve unacknowledged delivery; no professional result is invalidated by a reporting failure.

external_boundaries.content: For every run of the 13 selected Vera pipelines, Archive automatically prepares a schema-3 proof request containing product, receipt UUID, plugin version, canonical report SHA-256, existing Vera userID (installation_id), Archive run ID and report revision. The operational transport authenticates existing installation credentials and requires its existing verified machine link. Ordinary connection metadata also reaches Mparanza. No report body, outgoing payloads, source paths, source hashes, row counts, source values, prompts or model outputs are submitted. Verification supplies the receipt ID, report hash, Vera userID, Archive run ID and revision together. The replacement transport preserves the same closed reporting payloads. Browser cookies and optional original local credentials authenticate only; they are not diagnostic fields. Browser status and acknowledgements enter the selected host model context when the agent reads the rendered response. The schema view returns field definitions, not stored user data. The browser fallback sends no professional documents or raw model-data report.
controls: Only the fixed 13-pipeline scope generates new automatic Vera reports. Every selected execution gets a report, including full exposure and incomplete measurements. Start/end writes control collection; no agent-authored report input or substantive-work decision is used.

Vera records its own outgoing CLI, MCP and model-worker payloads locally before sending them, independently of host hooks and transcripts. Private internal results and MCP app-only metadata are excluded. The terminal Archive write freezes the local report immediately; a later result from a still-running operation is withheld if its pinned run or revision has closed or changed.

Vera schema 3 requires authenticated installation credentials and an existing physical-machine link. The public anonymous stamping route cannot issue this schema. userID, Archive run ID, revision and report hash are included in the Ed25519 signature.

The request uses one fixed HTTPS operational endpoint. Additional fields, mismatched owner identity, changed retry evidence, wrong-product records and verification mismatches are rejected. Local outgoing payloads are never sent.

Retries retain identical report bytes, UUID, version and revision. Professional artifacts are checked before and after updating only the reserved reporting artifacts in the Archive seal. Ordinary Archive use retries pending receipts and interrupted terminal reporting without re-executing professional work.

An explicit local_only option or local onboarding marker suppresses the proof request but keeps the report. Network or identity failures retain a pending receipt without invalidating the professional work. Host permission denials remain binding.

Verification proves the stored report hash, authenticated Vera installation/machine binding, Archive run, revision and server time. It does not identify a natural person or establish provider-side receipt, correctness of measurements, analytical correctness or GDPR compliance.
Historical schema-1 and schema-2 receipts remain readable through their existing routes; the authenticated Archive proof does not depend on a separate workflow-usage link.

The general verify command delegates schema-3 receipts to the same Archive verifier, defaults the expected owner to the existing local Vera installation identity, and requires exact agreement between the local receipt and the retained server proof. An explicit expected userID is supported for verification. Neither command rewrites the closed report or its professional artifacts. Legacy schema-1 and schema-2 verification remains independent of local installation credentials.

A saved terminal lifecycle transition remains acknowledged when local report generation or resealing fails. Report files are not deleted as a recovery action, unavailable reporting is acknowledged separately, and same-run retry finishes reporting without recalculation or duplicate lifecycle transitions. A partially written local report is not claimed as final before generation and resealing finish. Terminal recovery attempts are isolated and rotated locally; closure occurs after the local report and reseal succeed. Post-tool recording failures return operation, failure stage and a validated opaque run ID where available while withholding unrecorded case content. These metadata acknowledgements add no hosted recipient or server payload field.

Ordinary operations recover only the exact selected client/engagement/run; unrelated pending report locks and server requests are not prerequisites. Explicit maintenance retains the bounded independent recovery queue. Failed or cancelled runs may close using sealed ownership and retained observation evidence even when original or execution input bytes are unavailable. Execution, completion and professional-artifact seals retain their full integrity checks. No new recipient, payload field or source-file transmission is introduced.

external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza's fixed HTTPS Vera run-receipt endpoint and public verification page
external_boundaries.purpose: Authenticate the existing machine Vera userID and bind the hash of each selected Archive run report to that run, revision and server time.
external_boundaries.retention: The server retains the proof fields, server timestamp, signature and signing-key identity, with a unique userID/run/revision binding, without an automatic deletion period. Reports, exact Vera outgoing payloads, local database and receipts remain inside the local Archive run until the studio removes them. Deleting a server proof makes later server verification unavailable. Browser capabilities expire after 90 days; a separate public identity marker cookie lasts one year and grants no access. Transfer codes expire after five minutes and can be consumed once. Token/code hashes, original reports and linked history have no automatic deletion job. The form retains an unsuccessful request in its current DOM and clears it on success; it does not provide a durable browser outbox. The agent retains exact pending envelopes in existing permitted private task storage when available. The native reporter persists exact requests and receipts before and after transmission. Definitive schema rejections can be corrected under the same UUID; superseded rejected payloads remain private audit evidence. An ambiguous prior attempt cannot be replaced.

security_controls.control: The local collector accepts complete transport envelopes only when their exact digest matches a producer declaration. Selected row-field origins and private review-packet digests are retained locally, independently of send events; constructing them does not count as disclosure. A changed envelope, unknown private review packet or unregistered metadata parent cannot inherit the original declaration. Partial text reads cannot inherit complete-artifact lineage. Word body/table paragraphs and generated workbook cells use explicit producer origins for only the returned selection. Producer-owned JSON values also bind exact file bytes. The local argument-origin registry retains hashes of exact native helper argument strings under the existing run and component; it does not add a send event, read client files or submit these hashes to the server. Changed strings and a different run/component cannot inherit that origin.
security_controls.on_violation: The report retains the outgoing payload hash and marks source accounting incomplete; it does not fabricate an unsent remainder or prevent ordinary result delivery merely because provenance is unavailable.

security_controls.control: Both client and server enforce the same closed receipt request schema, and the server's Pydantic model forbids every unregistered field.
security_controls.on_violation: The request or response is rejected before a proof is accepted or written locally.

security_controls.control: Automatic Archive stamping and verification use fixed Mparanza HTTPS endpoints; operational credentials authenticate the existing Vera installation. The transport refuses redirects. The older generic receipt client retains its explicit loopback test option.
security_controls.on_violation: The client aborts before making a network request.

security_controls.control: The server signs the exact minimal record with Ed25519, including authenticated Vera userID, Archive run and revision for schema 3. A unique userID/run/revision binding prevents a second proof for different bytes. Conflicting receipt retries are rejected atomically; no report or source data are stored.
security_controls.on_violation: Missing keys make the service unavailable, invalid signatures are not returned as verified, and conflicting retries are rejected.

security_controls.control: Receipt routes cap body size and operation rates. Archive stamping additionally authenticates installation credentials and requires the retained verified device link; anonymous requests cannot create schema-3 proofs.
security_controls.on_violation: Oversized or excess requests receive an explicit 413 or 429 response without creating a receipt.
